summary: GitHub's official MCP server that lets AI assistants read code, manage issues and pull requests, and check Actions runs.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: The GitHub MCP Server connects AI tools directly to GitHub. It lets agents, assistants and chatbots read repositories and code, manage issues and pull requests, analyse code and automate workflows through natural language.
sixtySeconds.problem: AI assistants can't see or act on your GitHub work by default. This official server gives them structured, permissioned access.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for GitHub's own MCP server, available as a hosted remote server with OAuth or as a local Docker image with a personal access token.
requirements: An MCP host such as VS Code 1.101+, Claude Desktop, Cursor or Windsurf
For local use: Docker and a GitHub personal access token

overview: Use cases include repository management (browse code, search files, analyse commits), issue and PR automation, and CI/CD insights from GitHub Actions.
The remote server hosted by GitHub is the easiest route: add https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ in your host, sign in with OAuth or send a PAT header. An insiders version offers early features.

For hosts without remote support, run the local server from ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server with GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN set; keep the token in an environment variable, not in committed files. MIT licensed.
limitations: Access is limited to what your token or OAuth allows
GitHub Enterprise Server needs the local server

Sign in
steps.body: Complete the OAuth flow on first use, then turn on Agent mode.

steps.title: Store your token in an environment variable
Add the server
steps.code: claude mcp add github -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=$GITHUB_PAT -- docker run -i --rm -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server

environment.name: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
environment.description: Needed for the local server or PAT auth; keep it out of committed files.
